lessons.title: Artificial Insemination in Rabbits
lessons.body: Artificial insemination (AI) lets you breed many does without keeping many bucks. In Africa, where feed and space are limited, AI can help you use superior genetics from a single buck to serve 20-30 does per week. You need a teaser doe (a doe in heat but not bred) and a buck for semen collection. Collect semen using an artificial vagina (AV) warmed to 40-45Â°C. The buck mounts the teaser, and you collect the ejaculate in a tube. Dilute the semen with a commercial extender (e.g., Tris-citrate) at a 1:5 ratio. Check motility under a microscope; good semen shows 70%+ motile sperm. For insemination, restrain the doe in a breeding rack, lift her tail, and insert a pipette 8-10 cm into the vagina. Deposit 0.5 ml of diluted semen. To improve conception, give the doe an intramuscular injection of 20 IU PMSG (pregnant mare serum gonadotropin) 48 hours before AI. This induces heat and ovulation. Success rate can be 70-80% if done correctly. Keep records: date, buck ID, doe ID, and kindling date. AI reduces disease spread and allows you to breed from a buck that died if you freeze semen, but freezing requires liquid nitrogen, which is expensive. In most African small farms, fresh diluted semen used within 30 minutes works best. Train yourself with a vet or experienced farmer before doing it alone. Always sanitize equipment with 70% alcohol. AI is a skill that pays off by giving you uniform litters and faster genetic gain.

lessons.title: Genetic Selection and Breeding Programs
lessons.body: Genetic selection means choosing the best rabbits to parent the next generation. Without it, your herd will get smaller, sicker, and slower-growing. Start by recording every rabbit: birth date, weaning weight (at 4 weeks), 8-week weight, litter size, and mothering ability. Keep only the top 20% of does and bucks. For meat rabbits in Africa, aim for 2.2 kg live weight at 8 weeks. Select bucks from litters of 8+ kits and does that kindle 8+ kits and wean 7+. Avoid inbreeding: never mate father to daughter or brother to sister. Instead, bring in a new buck every 18 months from a different farm. Use a three-line rotation: Line A, B, C. Mate A bucks to B does, B bucks to C does, C bucks to A does. This keeps vigor. For disease resistance, cull any rabbit that gets sick twice. For heat tolerance, in hot areas like northern Nigeria or Senegal, choose rabbits that eat well and breed during hot months. Keep a herd book: a simple notebook with columns for ID, sire, dam, birth, weights, and notes. Ear tag or tattoo kits at weaning. Replace does after 6 litters or 2 years. Replace bucks after 2 years. If you want faster growth, cross your local breed with New Zealand White or Californian. But keep pure lines for replacements. Genetic gain is slowâabout 2-3% per yearâbut over 5 years you can double litter size and growth. Sell breeding stock to other farmers as extra income.

lessons.title: Intensive vs. Extensive Systems
lessons.body: Intensive rabbit farming means keeping rabbits in cages or hutches with controlled feed, water, and climate. Extensive means letting them roam in a fenced area or colony. In Africa, intensive is better for most small farms because you control breeding, health, and predators. A typical intensive unit: 60 does and 6 bucks in wire cages (75 cm x 60 cm x 45 cm) under a shade roof. Each doe needs her own cage. Feed 120-150 g of pellets per adult per day, plus fresh greens. Water via nipple drinkers. Clean cages weekly. This system produces 4-6 litters per doe per year, 6-8 kits per litter. You can raise 200-300 rabbits per year from 10 does. Extensive system: a colony pen of 20-30 rabbits in a 10 m x 10 m area with grass, bushes, and burrows. They eat forage and kitchen waste. But you cannot control breeding, so inbreeding and fighting occur. Predators (snakes, dogs, hawks) kill many. Diseases spread fast. Kindling is hidden, so you lose kits. However, extensive is cheapâno cages, less feed. In dry areas like northern Kenya, a semi-intensive system works: a raised wire floor pen with a roof, but rabbits get fresh forage daily. This cuts feed costs by 40%. For most beginners, start intensive with 3 does and 1 buck. Build cages from local bamboo or hardwood. Use a thatched roof for insulation. In hot climates, orient cages east-west to reduce sun. Intensive gives you control; extensive gives you low cost but low output. Choose based on your market: if you sell to hotels, you need consistent supplyâgo intensive.

lessons.title: Automation and Technology in Rabbitry
lessons.body: Automation saves labour and improves rabbit health. You don't need expensive robots; simple tools work. Automatic waterers: use nipple drinkers connected to a 20-litre bucket via PVC pipes. A float valve keeps water constant. Cost: $30 for 10 nipples. This cuts daily watering time from 30 minutes to 5. Automatic feeders: a hopper made from a 20-litre jerrycan with a PVC pipe delivers feed on demand. Rabbits eat 120 g/day; a 20 kg bag lasts 10 days for 10 rabbits. Solar-powered fans: in hot African climates, a small 12V fan (from a car) connected to a 20W solar panel keeps air moving. Place fans to blow over cages. Temperature above 30Â°C causes heat stress; fans reduce mortality by 20%. Record-keeping apps: use a simple spreadsheet on your phone (Google Sheets) to track breeding, kindling, and weights. Or use a notebook. For disease monitoring, a cheap thermometer and a scale (kitchen scale, 5 kg capacity) help you spot sick rabbits early. Weigh kits weekly; if a litter gains less than 100 g per week, check feed or disease. Automated lighting: a 12V LED bulb on a timer (15 minutes on, 15 off at night) can increase breeding activity in winter. But don't overdo itârabbits need 12 hours dark. For large farms (100+ does), a conveyor belt for feed is overkill. Instead, use a wheelbarrow and pre-measured scoops. Technology should reduce work, not add cost. Start with water nipples and a solar fan. Then add a phone-based record system. Train one worker to check automation daily. A simple 12V battery backup (car battery) keeps fans and lights running during power cuts.

lessons.title: Organic Rabbit Farming
lessons.body: Organic rabbit farming means raising rabbits without synthetic chemicals, antibiotics, or GMO feed. In Africa, this is easy because many traditional practices are already organic. Feed your rabbits with fresh forage: sweet potato vines, carrot tops, cabbage leaves, moringa leaves, and grasses like Napier. These provide protein and fibre. Avoid pesticides on forage; wash greens in salt water (1 tbsp per litre) to kill snails and insects. For feed, mix your own: 60% forage, 30% grains (maize, sorghum), 10% protein (soybean meal or moringa). No growth hormones. For health, use natural remedies: garlic and ginger in water for respiratory infections; aloe vera gel on wounds; neem leaf extract for mites. Keep cages clean and dryâthis prevents most diseases. If a rabbit gets sick, isolate it and treat with herbs. Only use antibiotics if a vet prescribes, and then withdraw meat for 30 days. Organic certification in Africa is rare for rabbits, but you can sell as 'naturally raised' to health-conscious buyers in cities. They pay 20-30% more. Breeding: select for disease resistance and foraging ability. Let does kindle in nest boxes with hay. Wean at 4 weeks. Grow to 2.2 kg at 10-12 weeks (slower than intensive, but healthier). Manure is a bonus: rabbit manure is high in nitrogen and can be sold as organic fertilizer. A 10-doe farm produces 1 tonne of manure per year. Use it on your vegetable garden. Organic farming costs less in inputs but more in labour. You must gather forage daily. But it's sustainable and appeals to export markets. Avoid copper sulfate and synthetic vitamins. Use seaweed meal or kelp if available. Always provide a mineral lick (natural salt lick).

lessons.title: Show and Pedigree Rabbit Breeding
lessons.body: Show and pedigree breeding is for farmers who want to sell high-value rabbits. A pedigree rabbit has a recorded ancestryâsire, dam, grandparentsâand often a certificate. Shows are competitions where judges score rabbits on breed standards: body type, fur, colour, and condition. In Africa, shows are growing in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa. To breed show rabbits, start with purebred stock: New Zealand White, Californian, Chinchilla, or Flemish Giant. Buy from a reputable breeder with papers. Keep detailed records: ear number, birth date, sire, dam, and show results. Mate only rabbits that meet the standard. For example, a New Zealand White should have a compact body, short ears, and pink eyes. Cull any rabbit with faults: white spots, long ears, or narrow shoulders. Feed a high-quality diet to get prime condition: 16% protein pellets, plus a handful of black oil sunflower seeds for shine. Exercise pens help muscle tone. Before a show, groom daily with a soft brush. Bathe only if necessaryâuse rabbit-safe shampoo. Trim nails. A show champion can sell for $100-300, compared to $10 for a meat rabbit. Pedigree kits sell for $20-50. To succeed, join a rabbit breeders association. In Kenya, the Rabbit Breeders Association of Kenya (RBAK) holds shows. In Nigeria, the Nigerian Rabbit Farmers Association. They provide judges and standards. Keep your lines pure: no crossbreeding. Use line breeding (mating cousins) to fix traits, but avoid close inbreeding. Keep a stud book. If you can't attend shows, sell pedigreed rabbits online with photos and ancestry. Build a reputation for quality. This niche market is small but profitable. Start with 2-3 purebred does and 1 buck. After 2 years, you can have 20-30 show-quality rabbits.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of artificial insemination in rabbit farming?
options: A) It eliminates the need for a teaser doe
B) It allows one buck to serve many does
quiz.explanation: AI allows a single buck's semen to be diluted and used for multiple does, maximizing genetic impact.

quiz.q: What temperature should the artificial vagina be warmed to for semen collection?
quiz.explanation: The AV must be near body temperature (40-45Â°C) to stimulate the buck and collect viable sperm.

quiz.q: Which hormone is injected into does to induce ovulation before AI?
quiz.explanation: PMSG (pregnant mare serum gonadotropin) induces heat and ovulation, improving conception rates.

quiz.q: What is a key record to keep for genetic selection?
quiz.explanation: Weaning weight is a heritable trait and a key indicator of growth potential for selection.

quiz.q: How often should you bring in a new buck to avoid inbreeding?
quiz.explanation: Introducing a new buck every 18 months helps maintain genetic diversity and vigor.

quiz.q: What is a three-line rotation in breeding?
options: B) Mating A to B, B to C, C to A
quiz.explanation: Three-line rotation avoids close inbreeding by cycling bucks and does from different lines.

quiz.q: In intensive rabbit farming, how much feed per adult per day is typical?
quiz.explanation: Adult rabbits eat about 120-150 g of pellets daily, plus forage.

quiz.q: What is a major disadvantage of extensive rabbit farming?
quiz.explanation: In extensive systems, predators like snakes and dogs can kill many rabbits.

quiz.q: Which system gives you more control over breeding and health?
quiz.explanation: Intensive systems with cages allow you to monitor and control breeding, feeding, and disease.

quiz.q: What is a simple automation tool for watering rabbits?
options: B) Nipple drinkers with a bucket
quiz.explanation: Nipple drinkers connected to a bucket provide constant clean water with minimal labour.

quiz.q: Why use a solar-powered fan in a rabbitry?
quiz.explanation: Fans improve air circulation and reduce heat stress, which can cause mortality above 30Â°C.

quiz.q: What is a cheap tool for monitoring rabbit growth?
quiz.explanation: A kitchen scale (5 kg capacity) lets you weigh kits weekly to track growth.

quiz.q: In organic rabbit farming, what can be used to treat wounds?
quiz.explanation: Aloe vera gel is a natural, organic remedy for wounds and skin irritations.

quiz.q: What is a good natural feed for organic rabbits?
quiz.explanation: Moringa leaves are high in protein and widely available in Africa, ideal for organic feed.

quiz.q: How long should you withdraw meat after antibiotic use?
quiz.explanation: A 30-day withdrawal ensures no antibiotic residues remain in the meat.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of organic rabbit manure?
options: A) It is toxic to plants
B) It is high in nitrogen
quiz.explanation: Rabbit manure is rich in nitrogen and can be sold as organic fertilizer.

quiz.q: What is a key feature of a show-quality New Zealand White rabbit?
quiz.explanation: New Zealand White rabbits should have pink eyes and a compact body, among other standards.

quiz.q: How much can a show champion rabbit sell for?
quiz.explanation: Show champions can fetch $100-300, much higher than meat rabbits.

quiz.q: What organization holds rabbit shows in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: The Rabbit Breeders Association of Kenya (RBAK) organizes shows and sets standards.

quiz.q: What is line breeding?
options: B) Mating cousins to fix traits
quiz.explanation: Line breeding involves mating related but not closely related rabbits (e.g., cousins) to concentrate desired traits.

quiz.q: What is the ideal dilution ratio for rabbit semen with extender?
quiz.explanation: A 1:5 ratio of semen to extender is common for fresh AI in rabbits.

quiz.q: How deep should the pipette be inserted into the doe during AI?
quiz.explanation: Inserting 8-10 cm ensures semen is deposited near the cervix for better conception.

quiz.q: What is a sign of good semen motility?
quiz.explanation: 70% or more motile sperm indicates good quality semen for insemination.

quiz.q: What is the recommended culling age for a doe?
quiz.explanation: Does should be replaced after 6 litters or 2 years to maintain productivity.

quiz.q: What is a good crossbreed for faster growth in Africa?
options: A) Local breed x New Zealand White
B) Local breed x Flemish Giant
quiz.explanation: Crossing local breeds with New Zealand White improves growth rate and meat yield.

quiz.q: What is a semi-intensive system?
options: B) Raised wire floor pen with roof and forage
D) Colony pen with no feeding
quiz.explanation: Semi-intensive combines a protected pen with fresh forage, reducing feed costs.

quiz.q: How much can automation reduce daily watering time?
quiz.explanation: Nipple drinkers with a bucket can cut watering time from about 30 minutes to 5 minutes.

quiz.q: What is a natural remedy for respiratory infections in rabbits?
options: A) Garlic and ginger in water
quiz.explanation: Garlic and ginger have antimicrobial properties and can be used as a natural remedy.

quiz.q: What is the typical protein content of organic feed mix for rabbits?
quiz.explanation: A 16% protein diet is suitable for growing and breeding rabbits.

quiz.q: What is a key record for pedigree breeding?
quiz.explanation: Ear numbers uniquely identify rabbits and link to ancestry records.
